lucas: Ran a randomized-prefix stress for ozma-14b-4q to probe speculative acceptance heuristics. Short notes + numbers. TL;DR: acceptance heuristic (early-accept on top-3 overlap) keeps misaccepts ~1.5% and gives ~12% p50 speedup, but tails hurt when rollback window >64 tokens.

maria: Nice. what did you randomize exactly?

lucas: For each input we choose a prefix length L from {8,16,32,64} uniformly, replace the next R tokens with high-entropy draws (R sampled 8..64), then run slot-based speculative (cheap sampler predicting R tokens and verifying). Measures: accept_rate, misaccept_rate, median latency vs baseline, rollback_cost.

tia: Can you paste the run command + summary CSV?

lucas: Sure.

```
# run cmd (simplified)
run_prefill_scan --model=ozma-14b-4q --quant=4q --scheme=slot-spec --random-prefix --trials=12000 --seed=7 --concurrency=300 --accept_heuristic=top3_overlap --rollback_window=64
```

summary.csv (cols: cohort,accept_pct,misaccept_pct,p50_ms,p95_ms,rollback_cost_ms,quality_delta_pct)
```
all_prefixes,21.4,1.52,44,160,32,-0.6
baseline_no_spec,0.0,0.00,50,185,0,0.0
L_small_only,31.2,0.9,40,140,28,-0.4
window_128,18.1,2.7,42,220,58,-1.3

```

maria: Interesting that larger rollback_window increases p95 significantly. Are those extra tail costs due to kernel recompile or KV-cache recompute?

lucas: Mostly KV recompute + some kernel spill/GC when window crosses 128 tokens. We see a bimodal distribution: small rollbacks ~20-30ms, large ones ~70-150ms depending on where we restart.

tia: How are we measuring quality_delta? unit tests or held-out benchmarks?

lucas: Held-out mixed eval: 65% NL QA (SQuAD-like), 35% codegen (short algos). quality_delta is relative exact-match / functional pass rate for code. Most negative drift is in code when misaccept chops identifier tokens.

anya: Any safety regressions?

lucas: Quick filtered check: no new safety hits surfaced. Misaccepts are almost always tokenization/identifier truncation or missing closing parens in code.

maria: Proposed follow-ups:
- Run selective canary: enable slot-spec with top3 heuristic for 5% of non-code production traffic.
- Add per-route rollback histograms to monitoring (buckets: <25ms,25-50,50-100,>100).
- Experiment with hybrid heuristic: top3_overlap + entropy gate (entropy < 2.5 nats).
- Investigate kernel warmup to reduce large rollback penalty (esp for rollback_window>64).

tia: Also try a cheap post-verify patch: if misaccept detected and last accepted token was part of identifier, prefer fallback instead of mid-recompute. Could reduce functional regressions for code.

lucas: Good idea. I'll add identifier-boundary check using our tokenizer flags.

anya: One more ask: can we replicate with concurrency=600 and R up to 128 to see stress on allocator and p95? Weekend run ok.

lucas: Scheduling that tonight. I'll push run scripts and raw traces to s3://redwood-experiments/prefill-rand/1789234567/ and open a PR with the notebook.

maria: Thanks. tagging @eng-releases and @devex for rollout notes. Closing for now. :white_check_mark:
